findings.message: The core/no-bypass exemption uses isReviewFindingsPath(target) with no task id and no phase check, so any task's findings path is exempt in every phase. The other-task block lives only in checkWriteWithinPlan and only in review. Scope the exemption to the active task and the review phase, or document that writes-within-plan is the sole judge outside review. The same applies to toolFormHit in self-protection.ts line 138.

The exemption in toolFormHit applies to every tool write verb, including delete, remove and move, so a tool-form delete or move of the findings file is no longer flagged by this check. The test covers only the shell form `rm`, which another detector catches. Exempt only the write, edit and create verbs, or add a test for the delete and move tool verbs.

BUG_LINE accepts only a single `- **Bug:** BUG-####` per staged line. A history entry naming several bugs, or other text on the line, yields no observed bug row and bugRowUpdated stays false. This commit's own entry lists only BUG-0124 although BUG-0128 is also fixed. Check the field grammar in SPEC §7.7 and parse every BUG id on the line, or confirm that one bug per entry is the grammar.

mergeBase takes the default branch with split('/').pop() on origin/HEAD's symref, which truncates a branch name containing a slash (for example release/1). The fallback chain ends at main, so it degrades safely. Strip the 'refs/remotes/origin/' prefix instead.
The entry fixes BUG-0128 as well as BUG-0124, but the Bug: field names only BUG-0124. The registry rows for both were changed, so the entry should name both if the grammar allows.
